Source: lodge-docs/REF-character-creation-summary.md, compiled from UNMASKED-players-handbook.md Part Two, GUISES-core-rules.md §1 and CREATION-identities-and-bonds.md

Core Rulebook creation — Identity, Theme, Origin, Attributes, Bonds — applies as normal, then the seven steps below.

Before the steps: what the first three actually are

  • Identity is a position, not a virtue. Brave is not an Identity. Poor Law Medical Officer is —

because it says which rooms you may enter, whose word you may contradict, and what happens to you when you are wrong.

  • Origin is where you are from. Whose accent, whose parish, whose church, whose dead.
  • A Bond is what you have staked in a person, place, institution or idea — up to three emotions, one

from each opposed pair: Admiration ⟷ Inferiority, Loyalty ⟷ Mistrust, Affection ⟷ Hatred. Strength is how many you hold. A Bond of Hatred is as strong as a Bond of Affection and works exactly as hard.

Attributes and derived stats

Dexterity, Insight, Might, Willpower, as die sizes: d6 → d8 → d10 → d12. d12 is the permanent ceiling. There is no permanent d20 tier — d20 exists only as a temporary, Check-only state.

  • HP = Character Level + (Base MIG × 5)
  • MP = Character Level + (Base WLP × 5)
  • IP = 6
  • Defense = current DEX · Magic Defense = current INS
  • Character Level 1–50

The seven steps

1 · The classes in your Innate Guises. These are you. Three classes to a Guise, ten Skill Levels apiece — that is the only count. You have two Innate Guises (human form and Other Shape), so up to six classes sit across the two, each Guise capping at 30. An Innate Guise may hold any classes, ordinary ones included — but the six Innate-only classes may only be placed in an Innate Guise.

2 · One Keystone. Your Quirk — the Rippertech graft that made you, an inherited relic, or another foundational aspect. One per character, ever. No two alike in the party. NPCs have none.

3 · One Torment. The shadow that lets you see — rolled or chosen, no two alike in the party.

4 · Two benefit picks, from the pool — or trade both for the Diabolist familiar. Locked at creation, never buyable later. The pool is ten items, one pick each: +10 HP · +10 MP · +5 HP and +5 MP · +4 IP · Projects · Rituals (Ritualism plus one other named discipline) · See You Later · Unexpected Ally · Personal Vehicle · the Diabolist's familiar (which costs both slots). Every pick is outlined on its own page — see The Benefit Pool. Any Skill available in the pool cannot be chosen at level-up by anyone. The four stat picks may be taken by any number of characters, and Rituals do not contend — Rituals grants Ritualism plus one named discipline, and any number of characters may name the same one. Everything else is one character in the party, full stop.

5 · Two Specialties. Write your own — there is no list. A Specialty is a short statement of something you are expert at, in your own words, agreed with the GM. When one applies to a Check, improve one die a size (never two Specialties at once). The Talented Keystone doubles it to four.

6 · One creation Heroic Skill.

7 · The Hunter Weapon. Your personal weapon — the only one that grows to level 50. Give it an origin.

Starting Bonds — a house rule

The printed game grants none. Here: three Bonds, four emotions between them, none above strength 2. At least one toward another player character, at least one pointing outside the party — a person, a place, an institution, an idea. The third is yours. These three begin solidified; Bonds formed in play are Fleeting until you spend a rest to solidify them.

Four emotions across three Bonds means one at strength 2 and two at strength 1 — a web, without a large number on day one. Strength 3 is earned at a rest, which matters here because rests are rationed.

Six Bonds is the ceiling. You cannot hold a Bond toward yourself, which is the printed reason your Torment is not one. Bonds are stronger than death — they persist after the target dies or leaves.

> Worth knowing before you spend them. In a Group Check, if any successful supporter has a Bond > toward the leader, the single highest strength among those Bonds is added — once, never the sum. > So a second Bond aimed at the same leader is worth nothing, and a leader gains nothing from their own > Bonds. For a party of four the efficient shape is a ring: A→B→C→D→A, one each. Everyone bonded to > everyone is six wasted slots.

What you start with, and how you grow

Five class levels to place across the classes in your Innate Guises. A step may be left unfinished — an unplaced level keeps, and you place it later.

Skill Level caps — the default: "If something doesn't list a skill cap, it's 1 Skill level." Any skill printed without a cap is max SL 1.

WhenWhat you gain
Every level+1 maximum HP and +1 maximum MP
Every level below 30One skill slot, added to every Guise you own — this growth stops at 30
Mastering your 2nd or 3rd class in a Guise*A Heroic Skill attached to that Guise*
Level 10Weapon and armour Clot maximum +1 each
